# Cosimo by Medici & Company

> Cosimo gives financial operations teams more capacity by taking on recurring work using their own records, procedures and reporting formats.

Cosimo is an AI agent for financial operations from Medici & Company. It brings source records through agreed preparation, checks and calculations into reports, review packages and follow-ups. The method is saved for subsequent runs with new inputs. The team resolves exceptions, retains professional sign-off and updates the process when requirements change. Principal examples are daily loan reviews for banks and investor reporting for funds; insurance and administration, accounting and advisory firms use the same approach for their recurring work.

The homepage routes visitors to banks (/banks/), funds (/funds/), insurance (/insurance/), and administrators and advisers (/services/).

## Platform

Path: /platform/

Cosimo is a hosted system built around AI models. Lessons are reusable procedures stored as SKILL.md folders, the same format as Claude skills. A lesson is private or shared, and every prior version is kept and can be restored. Memory works the same way: private or shared, versioned, and reversible. A team shares lessons and memory without syncing files. A workflow chains steps into one run and starts by hand, on a schedule, or from a watch. A watch detects a change in email, a calendar, Google Drive or SharePoint files, or a web page. Watches check at intervals; the shortest is five minutes. Cosimo works in a cloud sandbox that runs Python, installs packages, and builds spreadsheets, documents, presentations, PDFs, and HTML files. Nothing runs on a team member’s computer. A teammate runs a shared workflow from the web app with no terminal.

Cosimo runs frontier and open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock, hosted in the United States. They include models from Anthropic and OpenAI, and open-weight models such as Kimi K2. Low, Medium, and High effort levels map to different models, and small tasks go to cheaper models. An administrator can change the mapping, and each workflow step can use its own level. Token usage passes through at cost, or the client brings its own API keys. Connections cover Google Drive, SharePoint, Gmail, Outlook, and Google Calendar. A custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint is added by URL and authentication. Cosimo is registered as a Microsoft application, and a tenant administrator grants admin consent. A hosted browser operates systems that have no API, such as bank portals and state records, after the person signs in themselves. Client data stays in the client’s SharePoint or Drive and syncs in 30 to 90 seconds.

Verification: every figure traces to its source document and its calculation. Calculations live in a shared calculation library, so the same formula runs every time. A verified figure carries a mark, and a figure that Cosimo can’t verify goes to a person. The run history keeps each step, its transcript, the full output, and the calculation trail. Missing records go into a gap ledger, and Cosimo follows up on each gap before the next run. Conflicting versions go to the workflow owner. AI made preparing the work cheap and left checking it expensive: hours saved equal preparation hours removed minus review hours added. Cosimo is built so the person who signs can check the work in less time than preparing it takes. Dashboards are built from workflow outputs and edited by conversation. Auditor and investor views with restricted panels arrive in early 2027, so a controller sets what each outside viewer can open.

## Teams already building with Claude

Path: /building-with-claude/. Comparison guide: /guides/agent-harness-or-cosimo/

Claude and similar models can prepare financial work, and Cosimo runs Claude models alongside others. Teams building with Claude Code, skills, and connectors can bring their skills: a Cosimo lesson uses the same SKILL.md format. Most of a skill moves as written; connections and file paths need setup. A lesson is private or shared, and a builder’s existing MCP servers connect by URL and authentication. The comparison rests on questions the firm asks of its own build. Can someone other than the builder run it? Does it run when the builder’s laptop is closed? Can the person signing trace a figure to its supporting record without redoing the work? Who maintains it when a source format changes? Claude is a trademark of Anthropic, PBC. Medici & Company is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Anthropic.

## How a process is set up

Start with one recurring job, its owner, representative records and the output the team needs. Medici & Company configures the sources, calculations, checks, reporting format and review requirements with the team. Evaluate the output against its sources and the total staff effort across preparation, correction, review and follow-up. Record elapsed turnaround separately. Retain the agreed process for the next run and update it when requirements change.

Connections cover Google Drive, SharePoint, Gmail, Outlook, and Google Calendar, plus custom MCP endpoints. Task-specific setup and testing are required. An evaluation can begin with agreed file exports; connections to core banking, policy, claims, or accounting systems require a separate scope review. Cosimo does not currently have a SOC 2 report; a SOC 2 examination is on the roadmap. Data handling, access, retention, scope, and commercial terms are reviewed before starting.

## Banks

Path: /banks/

Loan activity reviews, borrower review packs, account-file checks, and review preparation are starting points for bank operations teams. The fictional Cabini Bank example contains a four-page morning review and inspectable source excerpts. It identifies a possible duplicate repayment, a difference from an independent closing balance, and an outstanding borrower certificate. The duplicate remains a question for the bank to resolve; the example does not post adjustments or make lending decisions.

## Fund overview

Path: /funds/

The fund overview introduces three recurring jobs: investor reporting, portfolio updates, and investor requests. An interactive example follows management accounts, company commentary, and a prior report format into a quarterly portfolio update.

The example uses Chianti Capital, the synthetic demo manager. Six companies report $70.0 million in quarterly revenue against a $72.0 million budget. Calderwood's accounts show $9.0 million while its management update says $9.4 million. The draft uses the accounts provisionally and leaves the $400,000 difference visible for review. The example has inspectable source records and a three-page draft. It is authored demonstration content, not a live application run.

## Insurance

Path: /insurance/

Renewal preparation, submission checks, claims-file summaries, and document follow-ups are starting points for insurance teams. The fictional Lanterna Insurance example contains a four-page operations review and inspectable source excerpts. It follows missing renewal documents, conflicting declared cargo values, and an incomplete claims file. Underwriting, pricing, coverage, and claims decisions remain with the responsible professionals.

## Administrators and advisers

Path: /services/

Administration, accounting, and advisory firms can start with client reporting, document collection, and review packs. Each process is configured around the firm's source records, reporting format, and review requirements. The responsible professionals retain client advice and sign-off.

## Real estate

Path: /re/

The page focuses on quarterly LP reports, investor statements, capital call notices, and distribution notices. The reporting example uses property figures, manager updates, and investor capital records for fictional Loggia Property Group. Visitors can compare source records with the proposed draft and explore a six-page sample report.

The example preserves open property questions and shows a simplified capital-movement schedule. That schedule excludes income and valuation changes and is not a complete capital account statement. Investor notices use supplied, approved allocations; they do not execute payments.

## Venture capital

Path: /vc/

The page focuses on preparing portfolio and LP updates from founder submissions, company spreadsheets, and fund records. Its fictional Telescope Ventures example contains six companies, five current submissions, one stale submission, and a company with six months of runway at its reported burn rate. An unsigned financing discussion is not treated as cash received.

The six-page example includes portfolio metrics, cash and runway, founder commentary, capital movements, and open items. Company operating figures are not fund performance or valuation measures. The sample capital schedule is incomplete until the necessary approved allocations and adjustments are included.

## Private equity

Path: /pe/

The page focuses on bringing portfolio-company financials, management commentary, and fund records into reporting drafts. Its fictional Chianti Capital example compares company actuals with budgets and explains an EBITDA shortfall from supplied management notes. Unexplained variances and unapproved operating plans remain visible.

The six-page sample includes portfolio metrics, budget comparisons, company updates, capital movements, and review questions. The company totals are management-reported operating figures, not ownership-weighted fund results. The sample does not implement an ILPA reporting template or constitute a complete quarterly financial reporting package.

## Private credit

Path: /credit/

The page focuses on private credit and direct lending: borrower review packs, covenant worksheets, reporting follow-ups, and LP updates. Its fictional Fiorino Debt Partners example follows six loans through servicing data, supplied covenant calculations, and a reporting tracker.

One worksheet shows leverage of 4.80 times using submitted EBITDA and 5.33 times if an unresolved add-back is excluded, compared with a supplied maximum of 5.00 times. This is a review question, not a determination of compliance or default. Another item identifies a missing borrower certificate. Cash interest received and PIK accrued are shown separately; neither is presented as the fund's net return.

The six-page credit pack is an authored example. Agreement definitions, adjustments, testing dates, and exceptions require the credit team's review. Lending decisions remain with the team.

## Hedge funds

Path: /hedge/

The page focuses on investor letters, close-file exceptions, subscription/redemption activity, and allocator response drafts. Its fictional Anamorphic Capital example uses administrator-approved figures and supplied policy records for a long/short equity fund.

The six-page monthly pack separates investor-facing drafts from internal working papers. It includes class returns, an exposure snapshot, investor activity, a cash discrepancy, and a questionnaire response that needs current supporting evidence. The example uses administrator-approved figures. The fund team resolves exceptions and approves investor communications, with valuation and sign-off responsibilities retained under its agreed arrangements. The page does not claim to perform trading, investment decisions, complete risk management, or independent assurance.

## About the examples

All interactive demonstrations use fictional records and prepared outputs. Interactions let visitors inspect the proposed document process, source records, figures, and review questions. They are not recordings of Cosimo generating these outputs, successful production proof runs, or customer results.

The examples explain the intended work. They do not substantiate a guaranteed processing time, hours saved, universal accuracy, autonomous delivery, audit readiness, or integration coverage. Each process needs configuration and testing with the team responsible for it.

## How to start

Email info@medici.ai with a few sentences about the report or process your team prepares, where the information comes from, and which part takes the most time. Medici & Company will work through a first process to test with the team. Scope, data requirements, an NDA, and commercial terms are agreed before source files are shared. An evaluation uses agreed source records, written feasibility confirmation, and a review of the output against its sources. Model usage is charged at cost without markup; platform terms are agreed in conversation.

## Customer fit and responsibilities

Cosimo is for banks, funds, insurance teams, and administration, accounting and advisory firms with recurring manual work. Fit depends on the specific process, records, and review requirements. Cosimo supports operations teams alongside their systems and advisers. For funds, it is not the administrator of record. Accounting, valuation, lending, investment, underwriting, claims decisions, and professional sign-off remain with the responsible people. Client data is restricted to that client’s work and is not used to train shared models.

## Actions and approvals

Cosimo can prepare work and perform supported actions through connected accounts. Sending to other people requires approval every time. Editing or deleting existing material requires approval too, unless a person saved a time-limited permission. Some actions confined to the user’s own account can be allowed on an ongoing basis. The specific connection, operation and approval requirements are established during setup.
